one_line: An agent-and-human physics experiment lab with live simulations, measurements, and trial comparison.
what_it_does: Runs projectile-motion and mass-spring experiments with shared controls, measurements, recorded trials, and comparison tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools appear to let an agent configure, run, pause at meaningful events, measure, and compare shared simulations more reliably than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists native tools for configuring, running, pausing, measuring, and comparing experiments.
Frame sheet visibly shows trajectories, parameter comparisons, graphs, measurements, and trial history.
The project explicitly targets consistency between visual state and precise tool responses.
execution_rationale: The evidence presents a coherent educational workflow with multiple experiment modes, visualizations, measurements, and recorded trials; the packet lacks a video transcript, so end-to-end execution remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows populated simulation, comparison, graph, and run-history views.
Description covers projectile and mass-spring modes plus live visual aids and trial notebooks.
impact_rationale: Physics learners and teachers have a concrete need to vary conditions and inspect evidence; the shared agent/human lab directly supports that learning loop.
impact_evidence: Description targets investigation of physics conditions and evidence rather than passive formula reading.
Visible prompt and measured comparison support an actual learning task.
creativity_rationale: The shared experimental environment and event-aware agent actions are a fresh synthesis for educational simulation, though the underlying physics topics are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent can pause at apex or equilibrium and inspect those events.
Human and agent operate on the same live simulation and trial notebook.
usability_note: The visible controls, graphs, and history suggest a usable lab workflow; no direct interaction test was available.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; some execution claims are packaging/frames-based.
standouts: Event-aware controls go beyond simple button automation.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible educational value with substantial visible product evidence.

one_line: Generates and verifies print-ready QR campaign assets and a production handover from one structured brief.
what_it_does: Accepts up to five HTTPS destinations, creates requested QR formats at physical size, reads them back, and reports per-placement verification and handover data.
leverage_rationale: The campaign-level atomic workflow, validation, generation, read-back verification, and structured partial-failure reporting are materially more reliable through a typed WebMCP call than browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies one create_print_ready_qr_campaign call covering the complete brief.
It validates before changes, generates at requested physical width, decodes outputs, and compares destinations.
execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually well specified and internally coherent, but there is no submitted video and no frame evidence establishing the live UI end to end.
execution_evidence: Detailed failure handling, SHA-256 fingerprint comparison, and private/public separation are described.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Print designers, marketers, and small businesses have a concrete production-risk problem; verification and handover directly reduce misprints and placement errors.
impact_evidence: Description identifies resolution, border, contrast, filename, placement, and read-back risks.
Outputs include verified files and a designer/printer handover list.
creativity_rationale: This is a practical and thoughtful extension of QR generation with a strong verification workflow, but the core category is established and the packet says the product pre-existed.
creativity_evidence: New campaign-level workflow combines generation, physical sizing, verification, and handover.
Editable management details are deliberately kept separate from public artifacts.
usability_note: The single-brief workflow and explicit failure reporting suggest good operational usability.
red_flags: Product existed before the challenge; only the added workflow is new.
standouts: Clear separation of public handover and private redirect management.
advance_reason: High practical value and meaningful WebMCP leverage despite limited visual execution evidence.

one_line: Lets analysts and agents search public comments, pin verified excerpts, and produce traceable cited briefs.
what_it_does: Searches Regulations.gov, organizes source excerpts on a shared evidence board, preserves human review decisions, and exports a cited brief.
leverage_rationale: Shared evidence state and structured pagination, quote validation, pinning, and export make agent research substantially more reliable and auditable than UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Description says agents search and pin exact excerpts while analysts verify or remove them.
The agent reads human decisions before preparing the cited brief.
Packet identifies API pagination and quote validation as core challenges.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent but there are no submitted frames or video, and the packet provides only description-level evidence of completion.
execution_evidence: Built-with list and live demo are reported.
Description covers search, verification, shared board, and cited export.
impact_rationale: Policy researchers and public-interest analysts face exactly the source-traceability and volume problem described; preserving review provenance has high credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets thousands of public comments and source-linked brief creation.
Human verification is explicitly kept in the loop before export.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-reviewed evidence board is a notably strong interaction model for agent-assisted public-comment research.
creativity_evidence: Agent and analyst share live evidence state and review decisions.
Unreviewed evidence is kept out of exports.
usability_note: The review-board model is understandable, but no visual evidence was submitted to assess polish.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or transcript; execution is thinly evidenced.
standouts: Good fit between WebMCP shared state and research workflow.
advance_reason: Exceptional impact fit and strong leverage; execution needs further observation.

one_line: An agent-assisted solar maintenance workspace for diagnosis, inventory, parts, and service tickets.
what_it_does: Searches stock, checks and updates inventory, creates tickets, tracks parts used, and generates restocking lists.
leverage_rationale: Structured inventory and ticket actions can reduce operational friction and improve reliability, but a capable general agent could plausibly perform much of the same workflow through the UI.
leverage_evidence: Description lists tools for searching inventory, checking stock, creating tickets, updating stock, and restocking.
The agent is positioned as an operator rather than a separate advice-only chatbot.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is plausible and the demo is reported alive, but the packet supplies no frames, transcript, or detailed evidence of completed flows.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
Description names concrete operational entities and actions.
impact_rationale: Solar technicians and operations teams have a clear recurring need to diagnose faults and coordinate parts and service work.
impact_evidence: Description is grounded in technician, inventory, and logistics tasks.
Actions cover the full path from diagnosis to restocking.
creativity_rationale: A useful vertical operations assistant, but the concept is a conventional agent-enabled maintenance and inventory workflow.
creativity_evidence: Combines diagnosis, inventory, tickets, and parts usage for solar operations.
usability_note: The scope is practical, but lack of visual evidence prevents judging interaction quality.
red_flags: Description is partially truncated and leaves implementation depth unclear.
standouts: Clear vertical audience and operational use case.
advance_reason: Credible impact, but leverage and execution are insufficiently differentiated or evidenced for advancement.

one_line: An agent-ready tender room where contractors price bids with traceable sources while a person retains binding approval.
what_it_does: Turns bills of quantities into structured tender workflows with price-book lookup, validation, human confirmations, sealed bids, and deadline-based comparison.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools expose authoritative tender state, role validation, blockers, and irreversible-action boundaries that would be difficult to reproduce reliably via UI automation; WebMCP is central to the product mechanic.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows the agent pricing rows, leaving unmatched lines empty, handling human-provided prices, and stopping at binding submission.
Tools disappear after submission and server-side sealing prevents premature bid comparison.
The page enforces validation and role boundaries rather than relying on the agent to behave.
execution_rationale: The long video transcript demonstrates a complete and coherent tender flow, including empty matches, expired certificate blocker, human fix, submission boundary, post-submission tool removal, and sealed bids.
execution_evidence: 167-second video transcript covers end-to-end contractor and property-manager flows.
Frames were submitted and facts report a live demo and public repository.
Server-side refusal and state transitions are explicitly demonstrated in transcript.
impact_rationale: Small construction firms have a concrete tendering burden; reducing missed tenders while preserving accountable approval offers substantial value to contractors and buyers.
impact_evidence: Description grounds the problem in bills of quantities, price histories, and time-consuming PDF work.
Workflow serves both bidders and property managers with sealed comparison.
creativity_rationale: The human-held binding click, role-specific tool surfaces, disappearing capabilities, and sealed tender state form a memorable interaction model rather than a generic CRUD copilot.
creativity_evidence: Agent cannot bypass final submission or expired-document validation.
Tool repertoire changes with workflow state and tender closure.
usability_note: Transcript suggests a deliberate, comprehensible workflow with clear waits and reasons for blockers.
standouts: Strong end-to-end evidence and two-sided tender model.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage, execution evidence, impact, and originality.

one_line: A Korean statute review workbench for exact, source-linked, date-aware agent retrieval and comparison.
what_it_does: Lets a person set statute, article, archive dates, and question while an agent searches, retrieves exact text, compares versions, and builds a cited brief.
leverage_rationale: Typed date-aware retrieval and exact article/version comparison reduce scraping ambiguity and make reproducible legal evidence retrieval materially more reliable.
leverage_evidence: Four read-only tools cover search, exact retrieval, version comparison, and brief generation.
Description emphasizes official and archived source links and preservation of the person's review boundaries.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the six gallery images likely support a substantial interface, but no video or transcript demonstrates the complete workflow.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete added/changed article example.
Facts report six gallery images, public repo, and live demo.
impact_rationale: Legal reviewers, researchers, and students have a real need for exact historical statutory text and verifiable citations; the tool addresses that specific risk.
impact_evidence: Description identifies current-version-only retrieval as insufficient.
Review brief preserves question, dates, changes, sources, and verification checks.
creativity_rationale: Date-aware source-linked comparison with a person-defined review boundary is a thoughtful, domain-specific interaction, though legal research tooling is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Historical article comparison classifies added, removed, changed, or unchanged.
Read-only design keeps the agent in an evidence-retrieval role.
usability_note: The defined four-tool workflow is clear; direct usability cannot be assessed without a video.
standouts: Appropriate read-only boundary for legal research.
advance_reason: Strong domain fit and leverage with credible gallery evidence.

one_line: A storefront co-pilot that searches inventory, proposes discounts, and drafts promo copy with live human review.
what_it_does: Registers three browser tools for read-only inventory search, bulk discounts, and constrained promo-copy generation, updating the dashboard after writes.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and visible shared state improve agent action transparency, but the described actions are mostly ordinary UI operations a general agent could perform.
leverage_evidence: Three explicit tools cover search, discount writes, and copy generation.
Every write updates the UI for human review.
Fallback deterministic copy and output limits improve robustness.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and includes a fallback path, but there is no video and only gallery/description evidence.
execution_evidence: Facts report two gallery images, public repo, and live demo.
Description identifies frontend, server function, AI limits, parser, and fallback.
impact_rationale: Small merchants have a clear overstock and promotion problem, and a constrained co-pilot could save time while retaining review.
impact_evidence: Description names overstocked products and lack of time for promotions.
Human reviews each write live on one dashboard.
creativity_rationale: A sensible human-in-the-loop storefront assistant, but the interaction model and concept are relatively conventional.
creativity_evidence: Combines inventory filtering, discounting, and generated promo copy in one dashboard.
usability_note: Visible updates and bounded writes suggest understandable operation, though no direct run evidence is available.
red_flags: No video/frame sheets; execution and tool invocation are not directly demonstrated.
advance_reason: Useful but conventional, with limited evidence and only moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: A territory-control strategy game where a browser agent plays through semantic WebMCP state while a human plays the board.
what_it_does: Runs seeded two-player matches with agent turns, validated phases/actions, combat, capitals, bonuses, and conversational turn synchronization.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: authoritative topology, legal actions, state, event history, and waiting turn synchronization avoid the fundamental unreliability of visual UI interpretation.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly says normal automation would need to infer geometry, adjacency, phase, and legal targets.
Agent receives a match contract, inspects semantic board state, and acts through validated tools.
A waiting call returns control to the same agent run for subsequent turns.
execution_rationale: The described game has a deep, internally coherent ruleset and reproducible boards; gallery evidence is present but no video transcript demonstrates a full match.
execution_evidence: Description names reinforcement, attack, fortification, neutral defenders, capitals, bonuses, dice combat, and victory conditions.
Facts report four gallery images, live demo, and public repo.
impact_rationale: Strategy-game players and people seeking novel agent interaction have a credible entertainment and experimentation use case; niche audience is valid.
impact_evidence: Human and agent have differentiated but fair interaction modes.
Procedural reproducible matches and personality/difficulty settings support replayability.
creativity_rationale: The two lands of interaction, where the human uses the board and the agent uses conversation plus semantic game tools, is a genuinely memorable use of WebMCP as gameplay.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP is explicitly a game mechanic rather than an automation bolt-on.
Turn synchronization lets one agent run continue across the human's turns.
usability_note: The explicit match contract and validated phases suggest a fair, understandable experience; direct play was not observed.
red_flags: No video or transcript; complete gameplay is not directly demonstrated.
standouts: Rich ruleset and semantic state model.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and standout creativity with a coherent game design.

one_line: A measurement-driven room and stair planner that tells shoppers and agents whether furniture can fit and where it jams.
what_it_does: Calibrates photos from known dimensions, derives stair/room geometry, simulates objects, exposes contextual tools, and supports cross-origin read-only furniture queries.
leverage_rationale: Tools expose precise geometry, fit answers, and blockage locations while dynamically registering only relevant actions; a general agent could not reliably infer these from rendered 3D/photo UI.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says the agent moves the couch to the exact stuck location using the same function as buttons.
Fit-dependent tools unregister when an object fits, and writes ask the person first.
Separate furniture site can query the staircase across origins through a read-only tool without account or API.
execution_rationale: The 156-second transcript demonstrates calibration, photo decoding, stair and room planning, object fit changes, tool lifecycle, and cross-site query; this is strong end-to-end evidence.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers actual measured stairs, couch failure, water-heater success, photo calibration, room reconstruction, and changing answers.
Frames and eight gallery images are reported, with public repository.
impact_rationale: Furniture buyers, delivery teams, installers, and homeowners have a concrete costly failure mode; advance fit answers can prevent damage and failed deliveries.
impact_evidence: Transcript grounds the problem in real couch and water-heater incidents and wall damage.
Output gives a shopping-relevant tightest-point measurement and exact jam location.
creativity_rationale: The combination of calibrated single-photo geometry, contextual tool registration, agent-controlled physical reasoning, and cross-origin staircase commerce query is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: No 3D scan or graphics card is needed for calibrated floor/stair planning.
The product exposes only contextually relevant tools and makes a separate website ask the staircase.
usability_note: The narrative and progressive measurement flow are clear, and human confirmation boundaries are explicit.
standouts: Strong evidence of dynamic tool lifecycle and cross-origin collaboration.
advance_reason: One of the strongest entries across leverage, evidence-backed execution, impact, and originality.

one_line: An adversarial multi-expert AI council with live citations, human steering, and structured verdicts.
what_it_does: Configures an expert panel and debate, streams web findings and citations, accepts human arbitration, and produces a validated summary and recommendations.
leverage_rationale: Native tools and human steering can make a multi-agent debate more controllable, but the packet does not establish that WebMCP materially changes outcomes versus a general agent using the UI.
leverage_evidence: Description claims WebMCP-native support and mid-debate pause/steering.
Outputs are Zod-validated and include cited sources.
execution_rationale: The feature set is coherent and eight gallery images are reported, but no video/transcript or direct tool evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo, public repository, and eight gallery images.
Description covers setup, investigation, arbitration, debate, and summary.
impact_rationale: Decision-makers and researchers can value structured dissent and source-backed synthesis, though the packet does not demonstrate the quality of the resulting advice.
impact_evidence: Specific panel roles and cited live investigation are described.
Human can redirect focus or end the debate early.
creativity_rationale: An adversarial council with live human arbitration is a fresh synthesis, though multi-agent debate and executive summaries are established patterns.
creativity_evidence: Four role-based experts debate and challenge assumptions.
Human steering occurs during the debate rather than only before or after.
usability_note: The staged setup and arbitration model appear understandable, but visual execution and result quality are unverified.
red_flags: No video/frame motion evidence; WebMCP leverage is especially under-evidenced.
Citations and debate quality are claimed rather than independently demonstrated.
advance_reason: Interesting concept, but insufficient evidence of WebMCP-specific leverage or completed execution.
